public_rationale: In the 2025-08-12 post, Marcus says that without a proper model, a system cannot reliably reason about time, inflation or changing prices, and can answer time questions only superficially. The quoted passage does not say what counts as a proper model. It sets no threshold for 'reliably' or 'superficially'. The evidence search did not find an agreed test of whether a system has a proper world model. It also found no benchmark that links reasoning about inflation or changing prices to whether a system has a world model. The search screened two sources: a temporal-reasoning benchmark in the NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks track, and a chronology preprint (arXiv 2511.14214). Neither sorts systems by whether they have a world model, so neither was used. With no definition and no evidence items, the claim cannot be scored as stated.
limitations: The case contains no evidence items, so no system's performance was scored.
The two screened sources measure temporal reasoning or chronology. Neither tests whether a world model is needed for reliable reasoning.
The search found no benchmark that links reasoning about inflation or changing prices to whether a system has a world model. The case does not show whether other research on price reasoning exists.
The quoted passage does not define a proper model, so the case does not settle what would count as one.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Without a proper world model, an AI system cannot reliably reason about time, inflation, or changing prices, only superficially.

statement.excerpt: Without a proper model, you can’t possibly reliably reason about time, and affiliated concepts like inflation and changing prices. A model might be able to answer queries about time, but only superficially.
statement.document_title: LLMs are not like you and me—and never will be.

from_speaker: you can't possibly reliably reason about time
and affiliated concepts like inflation and changing prices
A model might be able to answer queries about time, but only superficially
our_interpretation: This is a claim about necessity: reliable temporal and price reasoning requires a 'proper' world model.
Marcus does not define a 'proper model', and no public test separates systems that have one from systems that lack one. Without that line, the claim cannot be tested.
criteria.support_condition: Studies that use an agreed test for whether a system has a world model would show that systems without one fail reliable reasoning about time and prices, and systems with one succeed.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A system agreed to lack a world model would be shown to reason reliably and in depth about time, inflation and changing prices on robust evaluations.
